observations: Torah LM2 #120 is a five-paragraph narrative teaching with no explicit bechina language anywhere in the text. A new package requires at least 3 concepts connected by explicit bechina statements forming an independent thematic domain. This text contains zero bechina statements. The teaching's argument is structured entirely through eitza (causal) logic and one analogical simile: (1) improper use of kavvanot causes a sorcery-like spiritual damage — eitza; (2) focusing on the plain meaning of words causes devekut — eitza; (3) devekut causes closeness to God — eitza; (4) the comparison of kavvanot-misuse to kishuf is 'כְּמוֹ' (like), a simile, not a bechina equivalence. The four key concepts in the teaching — כַּוָּנוֹת, פֵּרוּשׁ הַמִּלּוֹת, דְּבֵקוּת, and כִּשּׁוּף — are connected only causally or analogically, never by shared essential nature. The teaching's themes (prayer, devekut, the danger of kavvanot) are extensions of existing prayer-related themes found across multiple LM1 and LM2 Torahs; this Torah does not develop an independent conceptual domain with its own bechina network. No new packages are proposed.
